title: Boston University (BU)
summary: Boston University (BU) is a university in Boston. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with BU.

sections.heading: What BU is known for
paragraphs: Boston University (BU) is a private nonprofit institution known for its diverse academic offerings and competitive admissions. With an undergraduate enrollment of 18,248 students, BU maintains a selective admission rate of approximately 11.11%. The university is particularly recognized for its strong business programs, which constitute about 16.19% of its academic offerings. Additionally, health-related programs represent nearly 4.97% of the curriculum, reflecting BU's commitment to fields in health sciences. These characteristics highlight BU's emphasis on providing comprehensive education across various disciplines while maintaining a rigorous selection process.

The average SAT score for admitted students is around 1480, reflecting BU's commitment to enrolling high-performing individuals. sections.heading: How to read BU tuition
paragraphs: Boston University (BU) charges a tuition fee of $68,102 for both in-state and out-of-state students. This uniform tuition rate means that residency status does not affect the base tuition cost. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition as well as additional expenses such as fees, housing, meals, books, and personal costs, amounts to $86,285. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and their families plan for the financial commitment required to attend BU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Boston University (BU) offers financial aid options to assist students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 19.15% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at supporting low-income undergraduates. Among students who complete their programs, the median debt incurred is $23,250. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use BU's net price calculator available at www.bu.edu/. Additional data on costs and aid can also be found on the College Scorecard website at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?164988.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Boston University (BU) demonstrates strong career outcomes for its graduates, with a completion rate of approximately 88.66% within 150% of the expected time. Graduates tend to achieve substantial earnings, with median salaries reaching $65,655 six years after enrollment and increasing to $83,238 ten years after enrollment. Despite these positive financial outcomes, the median debt for students who complete their programs is $23,250, reflecting the investment required to attain a degree at BU. These figures highlight the university's ability to support student success and long-term career advancement.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Boston University (BU) exhibits a diverse student body with a gender distribution of approximately 41.87% men and 58.13% women. This demographic variety reflects BU's commitment to fostering an inclusive campus environment. Additionally, around 19.15% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student population benefits from federal financial aid aimed at supporting low-income undergraduates.
